title: Using the `--log-file` arg with a relative path segfaults if the directory structure doesn't exist
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.7.dev, 4.6.2.stable, and older.

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.4255) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-1115G4 @ 3.00GHz (4 threads) - 7.70 GiB memory

### Issue description

Passing a log file path as an argument will only work if the directory structure already exists, or the path is absolute. Something like this will segfault:

`.\Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64.exe --log-file new_dir\custom_file.log`

Whereas this will work fine:

`.\Godot_v4.6.2-stable_win64.exe --log-file C:\Users\hwyrfel\Godot\new_dir\custom_file.log`

It also happens on Linux, so it appears OS agnostic. The problem seems to be that `make_dir_recursive()` fails, which causes `file` to be `null` when trying to call `detach_from_objectdb()`:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/137fa73ed4d71d2e7b3a53e2ab6b2690e1f46149/core/io/logger.cpp#L161-L170

Adding an if `file.is_valid()` check after `open()` prevents the segfault, although relative paths remain unsupported.

### Steps to reproduce

Run a project or the editor using `--log-file <path>` where `path` is relative and contains at least one directory that doesn't exist.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
